failure_summary.description: Ready searches or refinements were omitted, discarded, or not independently saved, including separate flight legs and locations.
The plan missed details established in context, including a party size, a hotel stay derived from a trip date and duration, or the return flight leg.
Cached results were only retrieved, already-covered criteria were resent, or the filtered result was not the object saved.
A minimum-only hotel rating was encoded as a singleton list rather than a lower/upper range.
Trajectories imported tools despite the runtime providing them directly.

patch.reasoning: The skill already covers cache compatibility, direct runtime tools, and separate flight legs, but these failures show that the execution checklist needs a stronger per-result completion invariant. The additions clarify how to carry forward an explicitly established party size, derive hotel checkout only when a stay duration is stated, preserve preferred airports across flight directions, and encode minimum-only ratings.

edits.target: - Bind the exact return value of every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call to a variable, then save it with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. Save refined results under a new key. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.
edits.content: - For every planned search, filter, sort, or nearest-results action, bind the exact return value to a fresh local variable and immediately save that object under a unique, descriptive cache key before using it downstream. Do this separately for each ready flight leg, named location, and refinement; never discard a result or save the prior/base object instead of the refined result. When filtering, apply only the new criteria to the compatible cached result. A retrieved result alone completes an item only when no new action or criterion is pending and that result already covers it. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.

edits.target: - For multi-city trips, preserve the stated destination sequence and match each date to its corresponding leg. Do not combine dates or invent arrival dates.
edits.content: - Preserve an explicitly stated preferred airport on the leg where it applies. Use the schema-supported origin-airport argument for an outbound leg and destination-airport argument for a return leg, keeping the user’s airport identifier literal even when city names are also provided.

For a pending hotel stay, when the conversation supplies a trip start/check-in date and an explicit length of stay in nights, use that date as check-in and compute checkout with `adjust_date` using the stated number of nights. Do not infer hotel dates from a flight date alone or from a date not tied to the hotel stay. If an assistant question states a concrete party size and the user answers without correcting it, carry that size forward as `num_people`; do not confuse it with the room count.

edits.target: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. Follow the schema for non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
edits.content: - Validate value encoding as well as argument names. For fields documented as lower/upper endpoint lists, represent an exact requested value x as `[x, x]`; do not pass a scalar or singleton list, widen the value, or treat it as a minimum. For hotel and restaurant ratings on the 0–5 scale, encode “at least x” as `[x, 5]` and “at most x” as `[0, x]`. Follow the schema for other non-exact bounds and do not invent endpoints.
